newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CREDITANSTALT TO LAUNCH HUNGARY FIRST FOREIGN FUND.
newsitem.headline: CREDITANSTALT TO LAUNCH HUNGARY FIRST FOREIGN FUND.

text.p: Hungary's Creditanstalt (CA) group said on Monday that using the opportunities of recent legal changes in the country it will launch its CA Foreign Currency Bond Fund later this month setting up organised way of investment by Hungarians on foreign markets for the first time.
Hungary's membership to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) in March paved the way for Hungarians to invest in foreign securities.

Hungary opened its market from July 1, 1996 to state bonds issued by the governments of OECD members and the bonds and shares of companies registered in OECD countries which hold the highest category credit rating in any of five large international credit rating agencies.

Creditanstalt wishes to invest only in government bonds, mainly in U.S. and German papers to get into harmony with the upcoming changes in the currency basket against which the Hungarian forint floats.
In the basket, now made up of 30 percent dollars and 70 percent of Ecu, the Ecu will be replaced by the mark.
"We wish to invest only in government bonds," Csaba Lantos, director for fund management at Creditanstalt Securities, told a news conference.
"We try to focus on the the most developed markets and the best debtors of the world," he added. "We wish to make investors to take the least possible risks."
The portfolio will also include some Hungarian government papers, to ensure liquidity, Lantos said.
Subscriptions will run from September 16 to October 18, with the minimum investment level set at 100,000 forints, Lantos said. The 10,000 forint investment notes will be issued at par value.
The fund, to be set up with a minimum capital of 500 million forints, will be transformed into an open-ended fund on July 1, 1997.
